attempt.consumption_boundary: The single authorized attempt is consumed when any analyzer, scanner, ranker, curator, selector, trace collector, or corpus runner first begins processing a real frozen corpus case. Synthetic fixtures and metadata-only admission checks do not consume it.

consumption_receipt.durability: The real-case entrypoint must create attempt-consumption.json with exclusive creation, canonical serialization, file sync, and parent-directory sync before it reads or processes the first real case; failure to create and sync the receipt prevents real-case processing.
consumption_receipt.point: canonical real-case entrypoint, ordinal 1, immediately before first real-case processing

control.scope: one trace-on result, one trace, and one trace-off public-result control for each of the same 30 case identities inside the single runner invocation

pre_attempt_requirements: exact corpus inventory and revisions verified
all bounded synthetic and focused preflight gates pass
no shipped change after the correction commit
exact corrected production artifact and public capability commitments match
attempt.retry_policy: No retry, restart, replacement, second trace, or second corpus attempt for any reason.

baselines: frozen D.2A report for historically available public fields
fields: TP, FP, FN, precision, recall, and every frozen score field
every field outside the correction boundary
requirements: integrity and completeness validation precedes effect measurement
every case and every candidate is compared
exact per-case and per-candidate evidence is canonically serialized
all protected historical evidence is byte-for-byte unchanged before and after comparison
the finalized attempt directory is byte-for-byte unchanged across finalization and comparison
strict historical equivalence remains failed-required-comparison-unavailable regardless of result

conclusions.correction-not-supported: Complete effect evidence disproves any required correction-supported condition or establishes that no public false positive was removed.
conclusions.correction-supported: Every condition in decision_conditions.correction_supported is mechanically true.
conclusions.inconclusive: The integrity envelope passes, but essential effect evidence cannot be completely established, including a preserved incomplete or failed attempt.

input: read only the exact frozen 30 corpus identities and revisions from the immutable schema-v2 cache
canonicalize and verify every input path before access
reject links, reparse points, non-regular required inputs, duplicates, escapes, and identity mismatches
remove Git metadata before analysis and use inspectGit false
never write into a corpus snapshot or corpus repository
never fetch, lazily fetch, invoke hooks or filters, execute corpus code, run package commands, or use network or model access
output: start in one previously absent evaluator-owned directory under the canonical operating-system temporary root
use exclusive creation and no-follow semantics for every directory and file
permit only regular files with one link inside the resolved attempt root
use ordinal trace filenames so untrusted case data never controls an output path
finalize additively into one previously absent eval/results/post-correction-attempt-sha256-<64 lowercase hex> directory
write comparison evidence only to a separate previously absent content-addressed directory
reject absolute paths, traversal, links, special files, duplicate identities, extra files, and bytes outside the declared inventory

correction_supported: exactly 30 valid case results and exactly 30 valid traces
complete schema, inventory, containment, binding, and hash validation
direct eligibility changes confined to package-declarations candidates with fan_in equal to zero, referenced_by equal to zero, and no entrypoint signal
every public change explained by direct exclusion or deterministic displacement
unchanged run/test commands, scan diagnostics, analysis errors, and categories
zero directly excluded labeled true positives
at least one public false positive removed

evidence_classification.score_status: diagnostic comparison only; no official score change

failure_policy.conclusion: inconclusive after the immutable failure envelope itself passes containment, binding, hash, and preservation validation
requirements: preserve every produced byte additively and byte-for-byte
create a canonical failure-manifest.json recording the failure point, observed files, hashes, and every missing required field or file
do not rerun or replace the attempt
do not modify tooling, production behavior, authority, protocol, schema, policy, configuration, labels, corpus, or acceptance rules post hoc
finalize only what canonical offline functions can rigorously validate and finalize
leave every protected historical evidence tree byte-for-byte unchanged

forbidden_operations: ranking, scanning, curation, selection, label, threshold, policy, configuration, protocol, schema, corpus, category, ordering, weight, or cost change
fetch, pull, merge, rebase, reset, stash, push, or remote mutation
corpus repository mutation or repository-controlled execution

attempt_failure.preserved_files: all files created before failure, without deletion, overwrite, rename, normalization, or truncation

limitations: does not establish strict historical equivalence
does not establish candidate-membership or scan-diagnostic equivalence with D.2A
does not establish independent, blinded, or causal evidence
does not establish an official score change
does not grant permission for another correction, corpus attempt, publication, or release

finalization: use only the already committed canonical offline finalizer and serializer or pre-attempt committed evaluation-only adapters proven byte-exact on synthetic fixtures
validate the staging attempt before additive finalization
derive the attempt directory content address from the canonical complete-tree commitment
create the final directory exclusively and copy exact bytes without transforming them
fsync files and directories before declaring finalization complete
hash the final directory and prove exact equality with staging
never write into the finalized attempt during validation or comparison
runner: invoke the existing canonical D.2E corpus runner exactly once

bind the exact clean committed pre-attempt HEAD, authority hash, corrected artifact, conformance, corpus, revisions, configuration, policy, thresholds, schemas, and invocation before the first real case
run all 30 cases in committed order with no --repo selection
use the corrected package-declarations implementation already committed
include the predeclared trace-on primary path and trace-off control in the same one-attempt structure
use the exact installed local tarball and immutable no-fetch cache
perform no network, model, corpus mutation, repository code execution, hook, filter, package command, or silent retry
trace: record every scanner-supplied candidate and every ranking and curation decision with deterministic identities
record no repository contents, excerpts, secrets, credentials, arbitrary environment, absolute corpus paths, repository URLs, label rationales, or unbounded text
sanitize and bound every generated path and reason
compute the trace-set commitment from canonical manifest entries in corpus ordinal order
validation: before effects, validate containment, regular-file type, single-link status, bounded size, exact inventory, unique identities, strict schemas, canonical serialization, hashes, and bindings
require exactly 30 expected cases and traces in corpus order
verify all completeness receipts and observer counts
recompute every file, trace-set, complete-tree, comparison, and evidence hash
verify all protected historical evidence identities before and after finalization and comparison
verify trace-on/off public-result exact equality under only frozen protocol exclusions
treat any mismatch as a P0 hard stop

serialization.hash: SHA-256 over exact serialized file bytes
serialization.numbers: finite JSON numbers only; counts and ordinals are nonnegative safe integers
serialization.object_keys: recursively sorted in ascending UTF-16 code-unit order
serialization.representation: JSON.stringify of the recursively key-sorted value with no insignificant whitespace, followed by one LF
serialization.validation: reject duplicate keys, non-finite numbers, unsupported values, malformed UTF-8, noncanonical bytes, and schema additions
